standard_prerequisites.name: A regular scheme is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes, and a normal Noetherian scheme has finitely many irreducible components, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement to the integral case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local rings of a regular scheme are unique factorisation domains, cited from the more-algebra chapter
For a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal and UFD local rings, the complement of an affine open is the support of an effective Cartier divisor, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the divisor whose associated invertible module is the candidate of the ample family.

standard_prerequisites.name: The invertible module associated with an effective Cartier divisor and its canonical section, whose nonvanishing locus is the complement of the divisor, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the nonvanishing locus of the canonical section with the chosen affine open, which is the cap condition for an ample family.

core_obligations: Reduce to the integral case: a regular scheme is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes, so after passing to a member one may assume the scheme integral, Noetherian, regular and with affine diagonal (proof lines 3561-3565).

Produce the divisor: for a point choose an affine open neighbourhood, which is dense because the scheme is integral, and use that the local rings are unique factorisation domains together with the complement statement to find an effective Cartier divisor whose complement is exactly that affine open (proof lines 3566-3572).

Read off the ample family: the canonical section of the invertible module associated with that divisor vanishes exactly along the divisor, so its nonvanishing locus is the chosen affine open; since every point admits such a chart, the two conditions defining an ample family of invertible modules hold (proof lines 3573-3581).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an integral scheme and, at a point, choose an affine open neighbourhood (proof lines 3561-3568).

Cut that neighbourhood out as the complement of an effective Cartier divisor using the UFD property of the local rings, and use its canonical section to verify the ample family conditions (proof lines 3569-3581).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-compact regular scheme with affine diagonal carries an ample family of invertible modules (statement lines 3553-3559). The counted proof is short but complete: it reduces to the integral case by decomposing a regular scheme into finitely many integral components, and then at each point chooses an affine open neighbourhood which, being dense in the integral case, can be realized as the complement of an effective Cartier divisor because the local rings are unique factorisation domains; the canonical section of the associated invertible module then has its nonvanishing locus exactly on that affine open, which verifies the ample family conditions (proof lines 3561-3581). It is H2: the reduction and the construction are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the UFD property of regular local rings and the complement statement for affine opens.
